canonical_title: Philip K. Dick Reviews Herman Wouk's The Caine Mutiny
author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: In a letter to Time magazine, Dick offered a terse, sardonic one-line verdict on Herman Wouk's bestselling 1951 novel The Caine Mutiny: 'The message I got out of Herman Wouk's Caine Mutiny is (a) Believe! (b) Work! (c) Die!
page_summary:
In a letter to Time magazine, Dick offered a terse, sardonic one-line verdict on Herman Wouk's bestselling 1951 novel The Caine Mutiny: 'The message I got out of Herman Wouk's Caine Mutiny is (a) Believe! (b) Work! (c) Die! What a hell of a message this is.' The remark condenses his objection to what he read as the novel's underlying message of dutiful submission to institutional authority into a blunt three-beat parody, followed by open contempt for the message he has just paraphrased.

**Why it matters.** Brief as it is, this remark is a clear, quotable data point for Dick's lifelong suspicion of narratives that ask their audience to submit to institutional or hierarchical authority without question -- the same suspicion that runs through his fiction's recurring interest in ordinary people who refuse compliance with corrupt or oppressive systems. Its appearance in a secondary profile rather than as a preserved standalone document means the full context of the original letter -- what prompted it, whether Time published it, and what else it may have said -- is not established by the evidence available in this corpus.

*The line is preserved only as a quotation inside a later piece of Dick scholarship; no primary copy of the original letter to Time has been located in this corpus.*
